read.notes: Nothing of the target survives beneath the gate: no title, maker, date or book. Kerouac's list is named, but as the composed entity, not bound to the piece as its model, so lineage is absent. The organic results mark seven of nine 'Missing: telepathic'; the one snippet carrying the word (ivanbrave.com, Essentials of Spontaneous Prose, 'telepathic shock') is the source of the title's adjective that the edition traces.

reading: The innocent reading first. Given the title without quotes, the Overview reads the query as a request for Kerouac's list, which shares every word of it but one, and composes a short account: a jazz-influenced method of spontaneous writing that bypasses the ego and transmits psychic energy to the reader, three 'core beliefs' and three 'technical rules', from Britannica, analepsis.org and a YouTube channel, with an offer to compare spontaneous prose with stream of consciousness. The organic results are Kerouac's list as PDFs, the Internet Archive record of You're a Genius All the Time, Open Culture, Jacket2, Literary Hub and others; Google marks seven of the nine 'Missing: telepathic'; the one snippet that carries the word is from a PDF of Essentials of Spontaneous Prose.
analysis: Without the operator, the title is read as Kerouac's with a stray word, and the stray word is the work's. The run is the retrieval-layer form of the misidentification the critical edition records at the composition layer on ChatGPT (btp-feist-reading-chatgpt-20261028): there the work is found and then displaced; here it is never reached. The results page carries the finding that matters for the edition: the one result whose snippet carries 'telepathic' is Kerouac's Essentials, where the word belongs to Kerouac's account of what spontaneous prose does to its reader. The piece's title therefore takes Kerouac's title and replaces its period word with a word from Kerouac's own poetics, and the composition, given that word, discards it.
d: BELIEF & TECHNIQUE FOR TELEPATHIC PROSE, UNQUOTED, ON GOOGLE AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT: the Overview answers Kerouac's Belief & Technique for Modern Prose, 'a jazz-influenced method of spontaneous writing designed to bypass the conscious ego and transmit raw psychic energy directly to the reader', with four of his items and two rules from his Essentials of Spontaneous Prose given as the list's. 'Telepathic' is dropped from the composition, and Google marks seven of the nine organic results 'Missing: telepathic'. The one result whose snippet carries the word is Kerouac's own Essentials, whose reader receives a 'telepathic shock'.

findings: SUBSTITUTED. The address names the piece; the composition names Kerouac's list and nothing else. No source, name or line of the piece appears in the panel or in the results shown.

THE ONE WORD DROPPED IS THE ONE THAT NAMES THE WORK. The title differs from Kerouac's in one word. The composition drops it, and Google's own result furniture says so on seven of the nine organic results ('Missing: telepathic | Show results with: telepathic').

THE WORD'S SOURCE SURFACES IN THE RESULTS. The one organic result whose snippet carries 'telepathic' is Kerouac's Essentials of Spontaneous Prose (ivanbrave.com), whose sentence on writing as deep as one wants ends on the reader's 'telepathic shock'. The adjective of the piece's title is Kerouac's own word, from the companion statement to his list; the retrieval found the source of the title's one changed word and composed from everything else (the critical edition, §5, title).

THE TWO KEROUAC DOCUMENTS MERGED. Two of the three 'technical rules' (the space dash; no correction or revision) are Essentials of Spontaneous Prose, given as the list's. The composition's own gloss, 'transmit raw psychic energy directly to the reader', paraphrases the telepathic doctrine of Essentials.
THE QUOTED ADDRESS'S NEXT STEP, TAKEN UNASKED. At the quoted title the Overview offers 'Detail Jack Kerouac's original 30 points' (btp-exact-aio-20261028); at the unquoted title it composes them.
